metadata.title: A methodology and modelling technique for systems of BDI agents
metadata.abstract_summary: A BDI (Belief-Desire-Intention) agent's behavior can be specified and validated through explicit external and internal agent models - roles, goals, plans, beliefs - before implementation, giving BDI systems a real design methodology rather than only a runtime execution architecture.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
sections.text: A BDI (Belief-Desire-Intention) agent's behavior can be specified and validated through explicit external and internal agent models - roles, goals, plans, beliefs - before implementation, giving BDI systems a real design methodology rather than only a runtime execution architecture.

sections.heading: Method
sections.text: Presents a structured modelling technique (an external agent model covering roles/responsibilities/interactions, and an internal model covering beliefs/goals/plans) and validates it by applying the full methodology to a substantial real-world case study, an air-traffic-management system, implemented on the authors' own dMARS BDI platform.

sections.heading: Evidence & Limits
sections.text:
- Validated by one substantial, real case study (air-traffic management), not a controlled comparison against alternative design methodologies.
- The underlying BDI theoretical claims - rational commitment, when an agent should reconsider an intention - rest on the authors' separately published formal semantics and are assumed, not re-derived, in this paper.
- Influential as one of the first systematic BDI design methodologies; later work (Prometheus, Tropos) built further structured methodologies partly in response to gaps this one left open.
